ai.definition: AI-exposed universe: a fixed, curated list of US-listed common stocks (registered on the methodology page), grouped by where each company sits in the AI supply chain: chips and accelerators, memory and storage, chip equipment, networking and optical, servers, cloud platforms, AI software and data, neoclouds and data centers, power and cooling, and a diversified group that includes a frontier AI lab. Membership is a judgement recorded in advance, not a measurement and not a claim that any company will grow; adding or removing a name needs a new methodology version. Foreign filers without US-GAAP XBRL (for example TSMC and ASML) cannot be scored and are left out. Every name is then evaluated by exactly the rules of the growth lists (price and fundamentals data, liquidity, Robinhood tradability, fixed-scale scoring with the same weights). AI large cap means a market cap of $10B or more and AI mid cap $2B to $10B; the top 5 of each are shown. Where a company sits in the AI chain does not say whether it gains or loses from AI growth, and none of this predicts that any company will rank among the largest.

private.note: Context for the AI page. Valuations are as reported by the named press or law-firm source on the date shown, are not from company filings, and are unverified. They are the value at the last priced round or announcement, not a market capitalization. A company with no valuation here had no figure corroborated by two or more independent sources when this list was reviewed.

ai.private_rule: Private AI companies are shown for context only: they are not ranked, scored or tradable here, and have no price, SEC financial statements or Robinhood tradability check. Each reported valuation comes from a named press or law-firm source with its date and link, is labelled unverified, and is the value at the company's last priced round or announcement, not a market capitalization. A record with a valuation but no source and date is rejected. A reported valuation is compared with the current S&P 500 market caps only when it is in US dollars. When a private company lists its shares, it joins the ranked lists only through a new methodology version.
ai.probability_note: No probability that any company reaches the top 20 by market cap is shown. A probability needs an out-of-sample calibration record (the methodology page lists the gate) and none exists for this question, so the page shows conditional scenarios and the scenario test instead.
ai.top20_rule: Top-20 market-cap test: the threshold is the 20th-largest market cap among the S&P 500 members that have valid data in the same weekly run (as-of close x SEC cover-page shares). For each listed AI candidate the test compares the market cap implied by its bear, base and bull scenario values at 5 and 10 years (value per share x the scenario's share count) with that threshold held at today's level. The threshold itself will probably rise over the years, so passing means 'above today's bar', not 'a top-20 company'. Scenario values are conditional on the stated assumptions; they are not forecasts and not probabilities.

multibagger: A 'multibagger' scenario here means a bull-case value of at least 5x today's price after five years (about 38% a year). A 2x-in-five-years outcome (about 15% a year) is shown separately as 'doubling'. For the long-horizon list the test also runs at ten years: a bull case of at least 5x (about 17.5% a year) and a base case of at least 2x (about 7% a year) within ten years. Scenario values are conditional on the stated assumptions; they are not maximum prices, targets or predictions.

rows.fees: No commissions, per-contract fees, regulatory fees or assignment and exercise costs are deducted: every payoff, breakeven and maximum-loss figure is before fees, so a real position loses slightly more and breaks even slightly later. probability.definition: Probability of profit = the probability that the position's net profit or loss is positive at expiration after the stated premium (ask x 100) and the stated costs (here: none). It is NOT the probability of finishing in the money: a contract can expire in the money and still lose money when the intrinsic value is below the premium paid.
probability.itm_definition: Probability of finishing in the money = the probability that the stock closes beyond the strike at expiration, ignoring the premium. Even this is not shown: no calibrated estimate of it exists here either.
missing_data: Historical option chains with bid and ask at each weekly as-of date: none are stored (Cboe provides current chains only, and option collection was off for every published snapshot).
Realized underlying prices at each contract's expiration, matched to the contracts that were listed: none, because no contracts have been listed and expired yet.
A model that records a probability for each listed contract BEFORE its expiration, so the forecast can be scored against the outcome.
An out-of-sample evaluation period of at least a year per option type and horizon with at least 200 resolved contracts, which cannot exist before the lists have run for that long.
Transaction-cost assumptions that match the broker actually used (fees are currently not deducted).
probability.never_substituted: Delta, the research score, the scenario weights and unvalidated pricing-model outputs (Black-Scholes sensitivities) are never shown or used as a probability of profit.
probability.statement: Probability not established — insufficient validated evidence.

definitions.market_cap: Market capitalization = the as-of closing price x common shares outstanding from the latest SEC cover page (dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding) filed on or before the as-of date, summed over the share classes the filing reports without class dimensions. definitions.universe: Large cap: current S&P 500 members (Wikipedia constituent list, CC BY-SA), whatever their market cap. Broad universe (mid cap and speculative): every common stock or ordinary share listed on NYSE, Nasdaq, NYSE American, NYSE Arca or Cboe BZX in the Nasdaq Trader symbol directories that is also in the SEC ticker file with a non-OTC exchange. Excluded: OTC securities, ETFs and funds, test issues, warrants, rights, units, preferred shares, notes, depositary shares, blank-check companies (names containing 'Acquisition Corp'), companies in bankruptcy, and companies without US-GAAP 10-K/10-Q XBRL data (most foreign private issuers file 20-F/40-F and cannot be compared on the same basis). Mid cap: $2B to $10B. Small cap: $300M to $2B. These lists cover the screened universes only: the large-cap list is S&P 500 members, not every large company. Speculative multibagger list: the S&P 500 and the broad universe together, $500M to $50B, passing every gate in its band definition. A company with several listed share classes (one SEC CIK) is evaluated once, using the class with the highest 20-day median dollar volume. Only stocks verified as tradable on Robinhood are published (see TRADABILITY_RULE).

entries.assumptions_note: Leveraged and inverse ETFs: the fund resets its leverage L daily, so its long-run growth depends on the path, not just the index's cumulative return. Scenario growth rate = L x mu - L^2 x sigma^2 / 2 - (L - 1) x financing rate - fee, where mu is the underlying index's arithmetic annual return for the scenario (its exposure-class total return + sigma^2/2) and sigma its volatility (trailing 3-year realized volatility of the tracked index fund; x1.25 in the bear case, x0.85 in the bull case). This is a constant-volatility approximation: real paths differ widely, and a deep drawdown may never be recovered. If the leverage, the underlying index or its price history cannot be identified, the scenario is unavailable. Tracked index proxy: QQQ; trailing volatility 20%.
entries.bear_case: A 3x daily-reset fund loses value in volatile, sideways markets even when the index ends flat, and a large index decline can cut it by far more than 3 times the index loss over multi-year periods.
catalysts: Direction AND volatility of the tracked index; low-volatility uptrends help, choppy markets hurt
invalidation: Index volatility stays well above its trailing level
Financing rates or fund costs rise materially
The fund changes its objective, leverage or is closed

watchlist.separation: The watchlist is a custom research universe imported from the owner's list. It is kept separate from the ranked growth screens: being on the watchlist never qualifies a stock for a ranked list.
watchlist.source: Ticker symbols the owner provided from their Robinhood watchlist on 2026-10-14. Tickers only: no account details, quantities, cost basis or balances. This list is NOT synchronised with Robinhood; edit this file to change it.
watchlist.statement: Conditional 2030 price scenarios: what the price would be on December 31, 2030 IF the stated assumptions held. They are not predictions, targets, guarantees or analyst consensus; the base case is not necessarily the most likely outcome, and no probability is assigned. Horizon = the actual time from the valuation date to December 31, 2030. All figures are PRICE scenarios (distributions excluded), on the split-adjusted price basis used everywhere on this site.
